name: Hotel Odhen's
signature_dish: Malabar fish fry thali — kingfish, squid, prawn and sardine fried fresh, with rice on a banana leaf
why_it_matters: Ranked #1 of 142 restaurants in Kannur on Tripadvisor (4.5/5, 200+ reviews), Odhen's is the city's most famous seafood address — a lunch-only, no-frills room on Onden Road in Kannur town where the catch is fried to order. Locals describe it as 'not a mess and not a restaurant' — a community dining space built entirely around fresh Malabar fish.
insider_tip: Open only 12-4pm and closed Sundays — go before 1pm or stand in the crush by the tables. Order by the fish: ayakkura (kingfish), koonthal (squid), chemmeen (prawn). It is on Onden Road in Kannur town itself, not in Thalassery.
signature_address: Hotel Odhen's, Onden Road, near Saranya Hotel, Kannur, Kerala 670001

name: MVK Restaurant
signature_dish: Malabar dum biryani — chicken, mutton or fish, Thalassery-style with kaima rice
why_it_matters: A long-running Kannur biryani house (the MVK group has served the city for over two decades) and one of the highest-rated restaurants in Kannur town on Tripadvisor. It is the everyday reference for Thalassery-style Malabar dum biryani without travelling to Thalassery itself.
insider_tip: Biryani in the Malabar style is the order — chicken or mutton; the fish biryani is a quieter winner. Several MVK outlets exist around Kannur (Talap, Chovva); confirm the in-town branch when navigating, and go before 2pm for the freshest biryani batch.
signature_address: MVK Restaurant, Kannur town, Kannur, Kerala 670001

name: Raandhal Restaurant
signature_dish: Malabar seafood platter — prawn fry, fish tawa and Kerala-style curries
why_it_matters: One of the most-reviewed restaurants in Kannur town (200+ Tripadvisor reviews), Raandhal is the popular sit-down multi-cuisine choice for visitors who want Malabar seafood alongside Indian and Chinese dishes in air-conditioned comfort — the everyday family-dinner anchor of the town.
insider_tip: Stick to the Malabar seafood — prawn fry and fish tawa — rather than the Chinese menu. It is busier and more comfortable than the lunch-only seafood institutions, making it the practical dinner option after a day at Kannur's beaches and forts.
signature_address: Raandhal Restaurant, Kannur town, Kannur, Kerala 670001

name: Indian Coffee House Kannur
signature_dish: Filter coffee with masala dosa — worker-cooperative cafe staples
why_it_matters: A branch of the Indian Coffee House worker-cooperative chain — a genuine Kerala institution run by its own employees for over fifty years. The SM Road branch is a reliable, cheap breakfast and coffee stop in central Kannur, with separate vegetarian and non-vegetarian sections and turbaned cooperative waiters.
insider_tip: Best as an early breakfast before sightseeing — masala dosa and filter coffee. Ask for the beetroot masala dosa, a quirk of the Kerala ICH branches. No-frills cooperative pricing; cash and UPI accepted.
signature_address: Indian Coffee House, SM Road, opposite Kamala International, Kannur, Kerala 670001

name: Paris Presidency Restaurant
area: Logan's Road, Thalassery — 22km south of Kannur
signature_dish: Thalassery dum biryani — short-grain kaima rice, the biryani style this town invented
why_it_matters: Formerly Paris Hotel — described in food histories as a birthplace of Thalassery dum biryani — and now Paris Presidency, this Logan's Road institution is ranked among the top restaurants in Thalassery. Thalassery biryani, made with short-grain kaima (jeerakasala) rice rather than basmati, is the most celebrated biryani in Kerala, and this is its home address.
insider_tip: This is in Thalassery, a 22km drive south of Kannur town — a worthwhile half-day biryani pilgrimage, not a Kannur-town walk-in. Order the kaima-rice biryani to taste the original; the fish biryani with white kingfish is the local insider pick.
signature_address: Paris Presidency Restaurant, Logan's Road, Paris Lane, Thalassery, Kannur District, Kerala 670101

name: Mambally's Royal Biscuit Factory
signature_dish: Plum cake — descended from India's first cake, baked here in 1883
why_it_matters: Mambally's Royal Biscuit Factory, established 1880 by Mambally Bapu in Thalassery, is where India's first cake was baked — a plum cake made on 20 December 1883 after British planter Murdoch Brown taught Bapu the recipe. The bakery still runs and gives Thalassery its 'Land of Cakes, Cricket and Circus' tag.
insider_tip: Buy the plum cake — the direct descendant of India's first cake — as an edible souvenir; it keeps well. The bakery is in Thalassery, 22km south of Kannur town, easily paired with a Paris Presidency biryani lunch on the same trip.
signature_address: Mambally's Royal Biscuit Factory, Thalassery, Kannur District, Kerala 670101
